name: IntakeQ/PracticeQ vs Jane App
title: IntakeQ/PracticeQ vs Jane App: Practice Management Comparison 2026
description: Compare IntakeQ/PracticeQ and Jane App for healthcare practices. See intake customization, billing, features, and which platform is best for your clinic.

summary.bottom_line: Both IntakeQ/PracticeQ and Jane App are Canadian-built platforms serving health and wellness practitioners. IntakeQ excels in customizable intake forms and assessments, while Jane App offers a more polished all-in-one experience with better Canadian billing integration. Choose IntakeQ for form flexibility or Jane for a complete clinic management solution.

sections.heading: IntakeQ/PracticeQ vs Jane App: Overview
sections.content: Both IntakeQ/PracticeQ and Jane App are Canadian-built practice management platforms serving health and wellness practitioners. IntakeQ started as a digital intake forms solution and grew into PracticeQ, a full EHR known for highly customizable forms and assessments. Jane App was built for multi-disciplinary clinics including physiotherapy, chiropractic, massage, and mental health, and is known for its polished interface and native Canadian billing. Both are HIPAA and PIPEDA compliant.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: IntakeQ forms start at $49.90/month (100 clients) with PracticeQ full EHR at $59/month. Jane App starts at $54/month for up to 20 appointments (Balance plan), with unlimited appointments at $79/month (Practice plan). Jane's AI Scribe is an add-on at $15/month per practitioner, while IntakeQ includes AI documentation features. US insurance billing is native to IntakeQ via Office Ally, while Jane requires a $20/month add-on.

sections.heading: Customization vs Completeness
sections.content: IntakeQ/PracticeQ's standout feature is highly customizable intake forms with drag-and-drop building, conditional logic, scoring, and branded client experiences. Jane App offers standard templates that are less flexible but provides a more complete out-of-the-box solution for multi-disciplinary clinics. Jane has native Telus Health integration for Canadian billing, making it slightly better for Canadian practices, while IntakeQ offers better US insurance billing through Office Ally.

sections.heading: Platform & Mobility
sections.content: Jane App has mobile apps and a more polished user interface, while IntakeQ/PracticeQ is web-based only. Both have similar calendar integrations (Google, Outlook). IntakeQ has superior Zapier integration for workflow automation. Jane App is better suited for multi-disciplinary clinics with diverse provider types, while IntakeQ is better for practices needing complex intake workflows and custom assessments.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your customization needs and practice type:

recommendations.when: You need highly customizable intake forms with conditional logic, custom scoring, or complex assessment workflows
You run a multi-disciplinary clinic with physical therapists, chiropractors, and mental health providers sharing one system
You're a Canadian practice wanting native Telus Health billing integration and PIPEDA compliance
You want to automate workflows with Zapier or need US insurance billing without monthly add-on fees

faqs.q: Which is better for Canadian practices: IntakeQ or Jane App?
faqs.a: Jane App has a slight edge for Canadian practices with native Telus Health integration for insurance billing. Both are Canadian-built and PIPEDA compliant, but Jane's Canadian billing features are more developed.

faqs.q: Which has better intake forms: IntakeQ or Jane App?
faqs.a: IntakeQ has significantly better intake form customization with a drag-and-drop builder, conditional logic, scoring, and highly branded experiences. Jane App offers functional but less flexible standard templates.

faqs.q: Can IntakeQ/PracticeQ work for multi-disciplinary clinics?
faqs.a: Yes, but Jane App is better suited for multi-disciplinary clinics with diverse provider types (PT, chiro, massage, mental health). Jane was designed specifically for this use case, while IntakeQ focuses more on customizable forms.

faqs.q: Which has better US insurance billing?
faqs.a: IntakeQ/PracticeQ has better US insurance billing with native Office Ally integration included in pricing. Jane App requires a $20/month add-on for US insurance billing and was originally designed for Canadian billing.
